cls: Second-generation cephalosporin antibacterial (oral prodrug of cefuroxime)
quick: 250 mg or 500 mg orally every 12 hours depending on infection (e.g. 250 mg q12h pharyngitis; 500 mg q12h skin infection)
May be taken with or without food (food can improve absorption)
Generally considered acceptable when indicated; weigh benefit vs risk
Excreted in milk in low amounts; generally compatible
Reduce dose/extend interval in significant renal impairment
No specific disulfiram-like reaction; moderation advised
Renal function, signs of superinfection/CDAD, clinical response
summary: Cefuroxime axetil is the oral acetoxyethyl ester prodrug of cefuroxime, a second-generation cephalosporin. After absorption it is hydrolyzed to active cefuroxime, which kills susceptible bacteria by inhibiting cell-wall synthesis. It treats pharyngitis/tonsillitis, otitis media, sinusitis, bronchitis exacerbations, uncomplicated skin and urinary infections, gonorrhea, and early Lyme disease. Key cautions are beta-lactam hypersensitivity (cross-reactivity with penicillins) and Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea.
indications: Acute bacterial maxillary sinusitis (adults and pediatric patients)
Acute bacterial exacerbations of chronic bronchitis (adults and patients >=13 years)
Uncomplicated skin and skin-structure infections (adults and patients >=13 years)
Uncomplicated urinary tract infections (adults and patients >=13 years)
Early Lyme disease (adults and patients >=13 years)

dosage.d: Per weight/indication (e.g. otitis media, pharyngitis); tablets and suspension are NOT bioequivalent
dosage.n: Do not substitute tablet for suspension mg-for-mg

admin: Tablets may be taken with or without food (absorption is enhanced with food)
Swallow tablets whole; the crushed tablet has a strong, persistent bitter taste
Tablets and oral suspension are not bioequivalent and are not interchangeable on a milligram-per-milligram basis
moa: Cefuroxime axetil is an inactive prodrug rapidly hydrolyzed by esterases in the intestinal mucosa and blood to active cefuroxime. Cefuroxime is a bactericidal beta-lactam that binds penicillin-binding proteins, inhibiting the final transpeptidation step of bacterial cell-wall peptidoglycan synthesis. This weakens the cell wall and leads to bacterial lysis and death. It is relatively stable to many bacterial beta-lactamases.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity (e.g. anaphylaxis) to cefuroxime axetil or to other beta-lactam antibacterials (penicillins, cephalosporins)
relative: History of colitis or gastrointestinal disease

preg: Cephalosporins, including cefuroxime, are generally considered acceptable in pregnancy when an antibiotic is indicated; available data have not shown an increased risk of major malformations. Use if clearly needed.
lact: Cefuroxime is excreted in human milk in low concentrations and is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding; monitor the infant for diarrhea or candidiasis.
renal: Cefuroxime is renally cleared; reduce the dose or extend the dosing interval in significant renal impairment, particularly with creatinine clearance below about 20-30 mL/min. Supplemental dosing may be needed after hemodialysis.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is generally required.

moderate: Probenecid (raises and prolongs cefuroxime serum levels)
Agents that reduce gastric acidity (antacids, H2 blockers, PPIs) - may decrease absorption of cefuroxime axetil
minor: Oral anticoagulants (cephalosporins may rarely potentiate effect)
interactions.food: Food enhances absorption; antacids reduce it
interactions.alcohol: No characteristic disulfiram-like reaction; moderation advised
interactions.diagnostics: May cause a false-positive Coombs test and false-positive urine glucose with copper-reduction methods

serious: Severe cutaneous reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis)

monitoring: Signs and symptoms of hypersensitivity reactions
Diarrhea (evaluate for C. difficile if it occurs)
Signs of superinfection (e.g. candidiasis) with prolonged use
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed and complete the full course even if you feel better
Swallow tablets whole - they are very bitter if crushed
Report severe or watery/bloody diarrhea, which may occur during or weeks after treatment
Tell your doctor about any penicillin or cephalosporin allergy
Report rash, itching, swelling, or trouble breathing immediately
May be taken with food to improve absorption and reduce stomach upset
pk: Bactericidal activity once absorbed and hydrolyzed to cefuroxime
Peak serum cefuroxime about 2-3 hours after an oral dose with food
Store tablets at controlled room temperature 15-30 C; protect from moisture
pearls: Oral prodrug - cefuroxime axetil is hydrolyzed to active cefuroxime; tablet and suspension are NOT bioequivalent
Second-generation cephalosporin with useful activity against respiratory pathogens including beta-lactamase-producing H. influenzae and M. catarrhalis
An option for early Lyme disease in penicillin/doxycycline-intolerant patients (500 mg twice daily x 20 days)
Food improves absorption; crushed tablet is intensely bitter
Cross-reactivity with penicillins - take an allergy history before prescribing
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue the regular twice-daily schedule. Do not double up to catch up.
overdose: Overdose of cephalosporins can cause cerebral irritation leading to convulsions, especially in renal impairment. Management is supportive; serum cefuroxime levels can be reduced by hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis. Protect the airway and treat seizures as needed.
